title: Prompt Perturbation Resilience Certification Procedure
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
This page defines the Prompt Perturbation Resilience (PPR) certification procedure: a deterministic set of tests, thresholds, and artifacts used to certify model+prompt combinations for production use at Redwood. The goal is to ensure features that rely on short-to-medium prompt contexts are robust to small, realistic perturbations (typos, punctuation noise, paraphrase, truncation, injected tokens) and to document acceptance criteria and remediation steps.

Scope
- Applies to any model, prompt template, or prompt engineering pattern that enters a Redwood production route (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Focuses on user-facing generation and classification workflows up to 2k tokens of effective context.
- Excludes deep multimodal transformations (see separate multimodal-resilience spec).

Why this matters
- Small prompt perturbations are a frequent source of regressions during model promotions and quantized deployments.
- Detecting and certifying resilience early prevents user-visible regressions, reduces rollbacks, and provides a reproducible acceptance gate for rollout automation.

Certification Levels
1) Bronze (SMOKE): Basic syntactic perturbations and truncation. Intended for non-critical features and internal tools.
2) Silver (PRODUCTION): Broader perturbation set including paraphrase and injection; must meet stricter stability and utility thresholds.
3) Gold (LATENCY-SENSITIVE): Silver plus adversarial paraphrase and long-tail stress tests; used for features with strict SLA and user impact.

Acceptance criteria (common across levels)
- Stability (Response Stability Index - RSI): median RSI >= level-specific threshold (Bronze: 0.80, Silver: 0.90, Gold: 0.95). RSI is the fraction of perturbations that maintain the canonical answer or acceptable semantic equivalence under automated similarity checks and/or annotator labels.
- Utility (Task Accuracy / BLEU / ROUGE / embedding-similarity): task-dependent; product owner must define the primary metric before certification run.
- Latency delta: p95 token-latency change versus baseline <= 20% for Silver and <= 10% for Gold.
- Token-economy: median synthetic token consumption delta <= 15% relative to baseline prompt usage for Silver/Gold.

Perturbation catalog (examples)
- Syntactic: whitespace shuffles, punctuation removal/addition, capitalization changes, repeated characters.
- Typographic: single-character insert/delete/substitute at random positions (edit distance 1 and 2).
- Structural: sentence reordering, short-sentence splitting/merging, truncation of non-critical context sentences.
- Semantic-preserving paraphrase: using paraphrase models or templates to rephrase intent-preserving prompts.
- Injection: prepended/suffixed unrelated prompts, user-provided strings with tokens that could be interpreted as instructions.
- Tokenization edge cases: broken unicode sequences, non-ASCII punctuation, surrogate pair boundaries.

Required artifacts for a certification run
- Canonical prompt template(s) and a representative seed set (N >= 200 for Bronze, 1k for Silver, 5k for Gold). Provide provenance: dataset source, date, curators.
- Perturbation generator configuration (seed, types, intensity). Example config snippet: 

```
perturbation_config:\n  seed: 4521\n  mix: [syntactic:0.25, typographic:0.25, paraphrase:0.2, structural:0.2, injection:0.1]\n  paraphrase_model: "paraphrase-small-v2"
  typo_rates: [0.01, 0.02]
  truncation_fraction: [0.05, 0.15]
```

- Eval harness job spec and runtime environment (model version, quantization profile, runtime flags). Include GPU/CPU profile for Dedicated/Private runs.
- Oracle / reference outputs: either human-labeled canonical answers or a curated golden-run set from a verified model variant.
- Annotator rubric for ambiguous cases and similarity scoring thresholds.

Procedure (step-by-step)
1) Prepare seeds: pick representative production seed prompts and annotate the expected canonical result or metric.
2) Parameterize perturbation generator: choose perturbation mix given target certification level.
3) Run deterministic perturbation sweep using eval-harness in batch mode. Record outputs, latency, and token counters.
4) Automatic pass/fail: compute RSI and utility metrics against oracle. If automatic thresholds pass, continue to 5. If fail, run triage (see remediation).
5) Human review: sample failure cases (min 50 or 5% of failing items) and apply annotator rubric. Recompute final scores.
6) Performance gate: verify latency and token-economy rules.
7) Rollout decision: if pass, create promotion artifact (promote request with cert metadata) and schedule canary rollout with increased monitoring.

Runbook commands and examples
- Submit a standard PPR run: 
  - CLI: rdinfer-eval run --job ppr --config path/to/perturbation_config.yaml --seeds seeds.csv --model vX.Y --out results/ppr-vX.Y.zip
  - Example JSON job payload: 
```
{
  "job_type": "prompt-perturbation-resilience",
  "model": "redwood/release-v10",
  "perturbation_config": "s3://eval-configs/ppr/silver-2026.yaml",
  "seeds_s3": "s3://eval-seeds/chat-assistant/silver-1k.csv",
  "expected_metric": "intent_accuracy",
  "run_id": "ppr-silver-20260305-asha"
}
```

Metrics and thresholds reference table
| Metric | Bronze | Silver | Gold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| RSI (median) | 0.80 | 0.90 | 0.95 |
| Task accuracy (relative) | >= 90% of baseline | >= 95% | >= 98% |
| p95 token-latency delta | <= 30% | <= 20% | <= 10% |
| Median token consumption delta | <= 25% | <= 15% | <= 8% |

Remediation and triage guidelines
- If RSI fails but utility metric holds: inspect failure clusters for formatting vs semantic drift. Prioritize prompt-template hardening (normalization, delimiter changes) and retry.
- If utility fails but RSI holds: this indicates perturbations change model behavior; escalate to model-onboarding team for candidate model re-evaluation or to request additional calibration data.
- If latency or token-economy breaches: profile with runtime profiler and check KV-cache effectiveness and tokenizer boundary handling. Consider adjusting batching/quantization profile or prompt truncation.
- Use the regression triage checklist (link below) to organize root-cause analysis: isolate perturbation type, compare to baseline seed-run, and run cross-model replay.

Ownership and SLAs
- Certification owner: Applied ML (prompt-sets & benchmarks) team.
- Execution owner (runbook): Evaluation Harness team.
- Escalation path: model-onboarding -> serving-runtime -> eng-sre.
- SLA for certification requests: Bronze: 3 business days; Silver: 7 business days; Gold: 15 business days (including human review).

Monitoring post-promotion
- Configure feature route to capture perturbation telemetry: store anonymized prompt diffs and hashed user inputs for 30 days.
- Enable RSI drift alerts: trigger if a rolling 7-day RSI drops belowCertificationThreshold * 0.95.
- Weekly stability digest emailed to product and SRE owners for the first 4 weeks after promotion.

Checklist before sign-off (must be attached to promotion ticket)
- [ ] Seed set and provenance attached
- [ ] Perturbation config file versioned and included
- [ ] Eval-harness artifacts (raw outputs, metrics, profiler traces) uploaded
- [ ] Human review samples and rubric decisions documented
- [ ] Performance profiling report attached
- [ ] Rollout plan with canary SLOs and rollback trigger points included

Appendix: similarity scoring and RSI computation
- RSI is computed as: RSI = 1 - (num_failing_perturbations / total_perturbations) after applying equivalence rules. For classification tasks equivalence is exact label match; for generation tasks we apply embedding similarity (cosine) with threshold T. Default T by level: Bronze 0.88, Silver 0.92, Gold 0.94.
- For ambiguous cases, annotators use a 3-tier rubric: Acceptable (A), Degraded but usable (D), Failure (F). A and D count as pass under Silver if D <= 5% of samples; Gold requires D <= 2%.
